reviewer_note: Agent review (Claude, AI agent) on 2026-11-23: side-by-side comparison of the extracted Arabic and English article bodies. NOT human-approved. Each note states what both texts say; no legal text is reproduced here.

articles.4: Both: employers and workers must adhere to Sharia when applying the Law.
articles.32: Both: recruitment from abroad for work requires Ministry approval.
articles.38: Both: no employment outside the profession on the work permit; worker may not change profession before legal procedures.
articles.59: Both: monthly-paid worker may not be moved to daily/weekly/piecework/hourly pay without written consent; acquired rights preserved.
articles.65: Both: worker duties beyond the Law - six numbered items (work per instructions; care of employer property; conduct; help in disasters without extra pay; medical examinations; confidentiality).

articles.89: Both: Council of Ministers may set a minimum wage on the Minister's proposal.
articles.92: Both: no deductions without written consent except six numbered cases (10% loan cap; social insurance; savings fund; housing scheme; fines/damages; court judgment capped at one quarter), with alimony first.
articles.108: Both: Articles 98 and 101 do not apply to four numbered cases (senior management; preparatory/supplementary work; intermittent work; guards and cleaners except civil security guards); Regulations set jobs and maximum hours for items 2-4.
articles.120: Both: Minister issues rules for part-time work; the Law applies only as the Minister decides, except occupational safety/health and work-injury protection.
